tips.comment: Western Diego looks a fine specimen here for Mullins and co. He finished second last time out in what was probably better company than this. With Danny doing the steering, he can get the Mullins train going.
Traprain Law has been out of sorts recently, but this is its track. It has proven itself with a good second here last year. Surely more ready now and will go close.

Top weight again for the 2nd year running. Now 1 lb lower than the mark he defied to win this event last term. He carried top weight and all before him when taking this race last season. Despite jumping slightly right throughout, he still had more than enough to fend off Traprain Law just for 2L, with recent Aintree winner Sans Bruit 6L further adrift in 3rd place. He's yet to trouble the judge in 4 runs this season. He's run well on occasion, just struggled off his lofty mark. He unseated rider LTO in a very competitive renewal of the Red Rum. He was still travelling well at the time, yet to play his hand. The yard must think he's sound enough to appear here just 9 days later. This looks to be plan B for them. If he's unscathed from his mishap LTO, then I think he can repel all challengers again this year.

Circumstances are very much in this lad's favor tomorrow, and his form has received a boost from Broookie's excellent 2nd at Aintree last week. Henry Brooke has won on him 6 times to date, and whilst other trainers' horses will take the market share, the value is with this lad.
The Other Mozzie had a decent win by 11L back in January at 2 miles but did not get on with the step up to 2m4f last time out. I think the return today to 2 miles could see him bounce back.
Won this race two years ago off ten pounds higher. Usually runs well in springtime and now tried in first-time cheekpieces. Looks cracking value.

LOUGHGLYNN is currently trading as joint favourite for this race. I wouldn't be surprised to see him go clear favourite come post time. He is the only runner from Mullins' yard, who won this race last year, and he's been pretty much winning every race on these shores for long enough now that it's always worth backing him to do it again. The drying ground should be a bonus as this horse has been a shade disappointing over the winter on soft ground. Jockey Sean O'Keefe has ridden him in the last 3 runs and should know what makes this horse tick. He still represents good value if going off near 4/1.

The stable tends to do well at this track, and I think this one has a touch of class. It can hopefully give weight all around after finishing an excellent 3rd of 20 to 'Jagwar' at Cheltenham (2m 4f 127yds) on Good to Soft Ground in what looked like a very competitive Class 1 Handicap Chase last month. Although 2lb higher today, it should hopefully have the class to see him come out on top.

There are wins and two runner-up spots from six starts this season. Only beaten by a half-length last time out at Uttoxeter. Goes on any ground and looks a solid selection for each-way purposes, receiving weight all around.

Handicapper has left his mark untouched, which is probably fair given his last run was rather due to poor luck rather than actual error. He was a strong candidate for the Ultima last time out. The choice of Derek Fox, he was hampered by a faller at the very first fence, which seemed to knock the stuffing out of him very early on, sending him to the rear. He could never recover from that, eventually pulling up. Stablemate Myretown went on to win that race in decisive fashion. This race looks less demanding anyway, so maybe a blessing his mark wasn't touched. He's won over course and distance too, which always helps around here, having won a class 3 handicap cosily enough back in January. Personally, I see this fella as a Scottish National type of horse. I think that will be the aim for him next term anyway. He gets a good chunk of weight from the favorite in here. I think he can win this on these terms.
This better ground will suit, and he comes here having been pulled up last time and has had a wind operation. Looks feasibly treated, and I expect a big run from him today.

If you take the second-placed finish of LORD OF THUNDER when finishing second behind Handstands in January at face value, then the 14/1 is massive. My horse was outclassed and 11lb 'wrong' with that horse, who went on to win a Grade 1 novice chase at Sandown.
Some good form over hurdles, but seems better still chasing with some good efforts and a few weak ones. Can bounce back here trying a longer trip.
Won its first 3 starts and then placed in some hot races, so probably has the best form on offer here and off the same mark as last time out.

Excellent effort when staying on for fourth place in the County Hurdle at last month's Cheltenham Festival. Looks the one to beat here if returning in the same form, with last week's Grand National winning jockey Patrick Mullins taking the ride. Another positive.
Let's go Bunting mental. Bunting was well fancied at Cheltenham and is a very good horse. He can really go well here for Mullins at a good price as well.

She fits most of the trends here. Ran at the festival last time out, which is a plus. Her last win came over 2M, which is also a plus. Fergal thinks the world of this mare. It's easy to see why. She's got very strong form to her name, despite running two lesser races the last twice. Her run in the Greatwood looks rock solid, running on similar ground to this. She ran a cracker to finish a 3L 3rd behind Burdett Road. She was sent off 85/40 favorite for that race. That tells you she's well thought of. The winner has franked the form since, finishing 2nd in the Champion Hurdle. She managed to rack up a 6-timer before that. She hammered this season's champion hurdle winner Golden Ace in her Grade 2 bumper win at Aintree. So clearly a classy horse. The ground is essential to her. She needs it faster, preferably. Mares don't do too badly in this race, with 3 of the 20 runners winning.
Looked a world-beater when winning at Cheltenham in October but hasn't backed that run up since. I just wonder if he has been saved for this by his wily trainer. I cannot resist backing him each way.

KIHAVAH has an interesting jockey booking with Brian Hughes stepping up for trainer Adrian Keatley. He is a mature type who arrives fresh having mixed it with some very smart even top-class hurdlers , so there are reasons to think this one could be overpriced.

CRACKING RHAPSODY stepped up in grade at the Cheltenham Festival and wasn't too far away, so I think he's been written off a little too readily here. Same mark, same jockey, same going, and some wins under the belt this season. Could be ready to take another step forward this afternoon and backable at the price.

Ooh Betty is a talented mare when ridden prominently. She has disappointed when held up twice this season. Her run at Ascot this season was full of promise, and she carries a low weight in a very competitive heat.
Another bet each way on the progressive in every sense Welsh Charger. He has 6 wins on his record, and today's good-to-soft ground should suit him perfectly
An unexposed horse who has done very well over the hurdles, won last time out, and is not any higher in the handicap with a try at 3 miles to bring out more progression.

Well backed ahead of this 3 miles mares' handicap hurdle, Armed And Fabulous is the sole representative of Willie Mullins (SR 23%) and commands strong respect on that basis. Looks well handicapped on a mark of 117 (carries 11-02). Off the mark in mares maiden hurdle at Newcastle last time. Step up in class and trip now but quite plausibly capable. Good staying pedigree from granddam Mr Combustible so 3 miles likely to suit. A bet at odds of around 5-1. Brian Hayes rides.
This one will finish within a length or so of wherever Foxys Fancy finishes and is a strong each-way bet. The form that won him last time out looks decent.

Lavida Adiva just kept winning last year but has been a bit down the pack since the return from a short break last October. But that was mainly running at 3 miles, and I think the return today to 2m4f could see her back in.

Has a chance of reversing form with Ruby Island, a pound better off for a neck beating with the two pulling well clear of the field. She is less exposed than the winner that day, and it was her first run for 5 months, and she was a bit fresh. Steps up in trip, which will suit. Big chance here.

Some really strong form when harshly beaten by Blue Hop. That race is working out extremely well, and this mare should be suited to the good ground, which others may not be able to say. I'd expect this to go close if running to form.

This looks like the best bet for the Mullins team, and this is the only reason for the bet, to be honest. Looks like a plot as it's so lightly raced compared to his other runners. Will stay, in my opinion. Looks like a great bet.

Steps right up in distance today. Running over 1M further than he's ever run over. His trainer knows the time of day. Surely he thinks this horse can stay the trip. The market tends to agree with that theory also. He's very lightly raced over fences. Just 3 runs to date, despite still being a maiden. He's run in much better races than this one. Stats tend to be against this fella. 5 of the last 6 winners of this race won LTO. Tbf, prior to that, only 2 of the previous 11 winners had won LTO, so that doesn't overly concern me. He won over hurdles at this meeting last season, just coming out on top in a battle to the line with Major Fortune. Tbf, he was giving 18lbs in weight to the runner-up. His penultimate chase run was fine. He finished a decent 3rd behind stablemate Champ Kiely. This fella is a former P2P winner and looks every inch a chaser. I'm hopeful this type of trip can unlock a vast amount of improvement.

Mullins bingo in here, but I feel like Spanish Harlem was worth siding with being 4 lbs lower than when 4th in this last year. He’s had his mileage steadily increasing over 3 runs this season, which culminated in a decent effort in the National Trial, which has seen the front 3 do something for the form. He might need a bit of rain to be seen to bear effect, but if he can be ridden a bit more positively knowing he’ll get the trip, I’d hope Hayes, who was desperately unlucky in the National, can smuggle him into this late on.

The inclusion of six from the Mullins yard just adds complications to this marathon chase. I have a feeling that he might be unsuccessful on this occasion. The Kniphand has the right profile for this race. He is just out of the novice ranks, looks steadily progressive, and put up a very good trial when finishing second in the Grimthorpe at Doncaster last time. He hasn't been over-raced, so should be fresh enough for this major challenge.

Rock My Way showed his capability at marathon distances last time at the Cheltenham Festival when 2nd of 18 in the National Hunt Challenge Cup Novices' Handicap Chase. He is still improving as a 7-year-old and should be in the first six home.
Looks like connections have targeted the Scottish National for SURREY QUEST if you look at how they mapped out his racing last year before finishing second in this race.

Probably rather foolishly taking on the legend that is Willie Mullins and his entries. However, trainer Nicky Richards has previous and won this in 2019 with his 10-year-old Takingrisks, ridden by today's jockey Sean Quinlan on board Famous Bridge. The 9-year-old Fame And Glory gelding ticks a lot of the boxes. He has 7 wins and 5 places from 20 jump races, with 5 wins and 3 places coming from just 14 chase runs. He is a course winner and will love the ground and has won and placed in this grade. All in all, at 22/1, he's my e/w play.
This horse is an out-and-out stayer who won well last time out over 3 miles and 4 furlongs. Carries a featherweight and will be running on when many have cried enough.

Won off 136 around here on good ground 2 years ago. Has been hit and miss since and has bled, which is a worry, but he ran well last time and is well in on old form off just 132. Has an each-way chance.

I like the look of Captain Cody in this for Willie Mullins, and the booking of Harry Cobden looks interesting. He has performed at a high level and was disappointed at Cheltenham to run into some trouble when traveling nicely. Can go close here. Maybe each way is the way to go.

3/11 winning favorites, 4/11 top 3 in the betting. 10/11 carried 10st - 11st3. Won 2 on the bounce before 4th to Victtorino in the 3m Swinley handicap. Followed that up by running a decent race in 3rd when he fell at the last in the NH Cup at Cheltenham. That was 3m6f and could expect the extra distance to bring about even more improvement. Novice chasers have a strong record in this.

Macdermott won for the Mullins team this time last year. Although he hasn't had much of a season to shout about, the master trainer will have him in ship shape. With Danny back on board, he can get the best out of him.
Wiseguy is from the top Henderson stable. The horse has won two of his six chase runs. This extra distance should suit the horse fine.

Klarc Kent is very interesting, running for the Grand National-winning stable of Willie Mullins (SR 24%). Fourth in this race last year, staying on at the finish, and runs here off a mark eight pounds lower, carrying only 10-02. Jonathan Burke (SR 15%) rides. It's the low weight that makes this horse a bet, 12 pounds lower than all his stablemates. Likely to have had a very similar preparation for this race.

Magna Sam is almost 11 years-old but he showed he is an evergreen equine when winning the Edinburgh National in February in first-time cheekpieces (worn again) - besides, Red Rum was 12 when he won his third Grand National. Magna Sam was third in this event in 2023 off a mark of 125 and runs off 3 pounds lower today. He stays the marathon trip, acts on the going and has won 5 from 20 races over fences. So plenty of boxes ticked. With 6 places on offer 25/1 looks most appealing.
Flash De Touzaine finished 4th in this very race two years ago. Won well last time out and can reward each way support in this race.

I'll take a look at SNIPE in the Scottish Grand National. He has performed well at this level when seen at Doncaster in January and seems to be shaping up to be suited by further. Dipped slightly the last two times, but the claimer takes some weight off and could be a threat from a big price if back in the mood he was in at the start of the year.

Our Power has won each of his last 3 chases on good ground, and that looks to be the key here where many of his rivals would prefer some cut. The excellent 3lb claiming Conditional Dylan Johnston has been booked for the last 3 rides and been placed each time over inadequate trips. The horse was going well in the 2023 Grand National until stumbling badly 2 out and losing all chance, but that was a clear indication that he could well be suited by this extreme test of stamina.

GROZNI looks a huge price here at 50/1. The selection ran a very respectable 6th in the Kim Muir at Cheltenham off a mark of 129. He's been dropped 2lb by the handicapper for this and has a 5lb claimer onboard. The step up in trip is an unknown but he was outpaced 4f out last time out over 3m 2f, so the extra 5f should help.

Been stung by this horse before when he refuses to run/compete. Talented horse on his day, has proven that he can stay the trip with a strong 2nd at Uttoxeter on 16/3/24 over 4m 2f at the Midlands Grand National. If (big if) he wants to run, he can get top 6. Different jockey this time, also claiming 3lb.

Jump Allen won cosily on handicap debut last time from a mark of 114, winning by 4.5L with the same distance back to the 3rd. He's effectively 14lbs higher here but won readily and steps up in trip today for his superstar yard that won this last year. Jockey retained in the saddle and with UK prize money on offer he'll be primed to follow up from a mark of 128.

Handicap debut and step up in trip looks sure to suit as plenty of stamina on the dam's side of pedigree. Yard did well at Ayr today with a winner and a well backed second from two runners. Jockey rides track well and though is only 5-48 here this season does return a plus £10 lsp. Was second in a bumper and on hurdles debut here at Ayr before winning in good style at the stiff Hexham so looks sure to appreciate this longer trip. Looks a cracking each way play at the prices and won't mind drying ground either.

Race 6 at Ayr today is the Stagecoach We've Got You Novices' Handicap Hurdle (Class 3) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 4,892 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 6-year-old gelding Quebecois from the Paul Nicholls yard and will be ridden by Harry Cobden. This son of No Risk At All is a two-time winner from 6 starts and is also a two-time runner-up, once at Gr2 level. He must have some sort of chance in today's small lineup.

Sets the standard here after 2nd place in Grade 2 at Kelso 42 days ago, beaten 2.5L to Jet To Vegas, who subsequently disappointed at Aintree. But that was over 18f. Today's step up to 21f should suit, and drying ground is no worry.

The model I run simulates this race and has The Jukebox Kid coming in first. This is predominantly driven by good form figures of 1-1, 2 lbs less weight to carry, and looks well treated. Previous wins have both come on 2m 4f distance, compared to Chart Topper who is yet to go further than 2m 2f.

The Irish have won this four times in a row, and Mullins has probably picked his best here. Even though unraced, he wouldn't be putting them in if he didn't think they could win. We know how good he is with a race like this.

Beyond The Verge hasn't been seen over the winter, presumably to avoid the worst of the ground ahead of a spring campaign. The yard had a poor winter so not running will have been a bonus. The Susan Corbett team have been in great form lately and very often have winners, and placed runners, at big prices. I could see this one outrunning his generous looking odds.

BELLUM JUSTUM is the only notable horse in the field to have won on reappearance last season and finished the season high with a big payout in Kentucky. Sired by SEA THE STARS, I expect that stamina and quality to be too strong for the French raider with all horses reappearing for the first time this season.

Feigning Madness is a 4-year-old gelding trained by Ralph Beckett. He is 2/4 wins and has posted a career-high RPR of 98, so he has a bit to find on official ratings. It's interesting that he resumes at this level and has possibly shown a bit at home in training. Ralph Beckett does well in Group 3 12f races at Newbury with 6/22 wins and 12/22 placed. Interesting under Hector Crouch.

Took his chance in the Derby over this trip last year but finished 14th of 16 and was well beaten. Not seen again after that race until justifying favoritism when winning over a mile and a quarter at Dundalk in February. Last seen over that same trip at Naas 20 days ago. Will be a lot fitter following those two runs, unlike the rest of the field, and could surprise with that race fitness edge.

Mountain Breeze arrives in top form after two easy wins at Meydan and already has solid Group form in the book from last season. She’s a close relative of Pinatubo and clearly has plenty of class. With the trainer and jockey combination showing profit at Newbury (69 runs, 25 wins, 1.09 A/E, +14pts @ 20% ROI), she’s a big player and should be tough to beat if she brings that Dubai form back with her.
Simmering, I think she sets the standard for this, having won in G2 and G3 last year. Plus, I am a big fan of having Christophe Soumillon in the saddle, and expectations are high.

Bright Times Ahead is a 3-year-old filly trained by Ralph Beckett. She was a ready winner at Newmarket, beating Gosden and Appleby horses by 3.5 lengths. She is a promising filly whose trainer has landed this race five times. She is related to four horses who placed or won pattern races, so she has a nice pedigree and should contend under Rossa Ryan.

Winner on the all-weather on racecourse debut last season before finishing in the places on both subsequent outings. Stayed on well when denied a second win over six furlongs in a Group Two last time out. Today's extra furlong looks ideal and looks to have strong claims here with no concerns about today's underfoot conditions.
Formal won first time out at Newbury on Good to Firm last year when trained by M Stoute and now with the Balding stable and hood fitted, she will not want for fitness.

Fillies in April. No, it is not a song, but it is almost impossible to judge how they have progressed into their 3rd year until you see it on a racecourse. It is highly probable who, despite what I consider a poor winter, have done well. California Dreamer won a maiden with the minimum of fuss at 1/6 in February, so should be fairly fit. It also ran some highly creditable races last year, notably behind the unfortunate Fairy Godmother, and as such merits a small bet.
This horse has posted some very good figures, and I feel it is a lot better than the odds suggest. Maybe a little outclassed, but hard to ignore at the odds.

Al Qudra might not have the same long-term potential as a couple of these but he’s already a Listed winner at two and looked sharp when winning on his return in Qatar. He’s race-fit and knows how to get the job done, and with a trainer and jockey combo that shows profit at Newbury (69 runs, 25 wins, 1.09 A/E, +14pts @ 20% ROI), he could easily make his presence felt here.

Rashabar sets the standard the rest have to reach with his 5 starts as a juvenile, including winning the Group 2 Coventry before being touched off in a pair of Group 1s. The latest of which was having been stepped up to 7f. His yard won this two years ago with Isaac Shelby - also the class horse in the field - and conditions will be fine, having won at Royal Ascot on good to firm, but his two G1 2nds have had a bit more cut in the ground.
Slow start in most recent race, ran well but struggled to offer more when asked, was a quick race overall. First run for new yard and horse will be nice and fresh. Elite jockey on board.

NOBLE CHAMPION could be a dark horse who is set to enjoy a solid season now as a three year old. He learned plenty from his modest debut run as a juvenile and trainer Ed Walker can get a young horse to improve rapidly. Related to a seven furlong useful type and worth considering.

Aurora Majesty is a 3yo Night of Thunder colt who is two from two now having won a couple of AW maidens last month, each over seven furlongs. Strongly supported in the market on debut suggesting had showed considerable promise at home. Hollie Doyle rode the Archie Watson trained colt on each occasion (both ready wins) and is back up today. Would be a surprise Greenham winner but 66-1 looks too big a price in ultimately quite an open race.

SON runs for trainer Richard Hannon who generally does well with those he sends to Newbury. This four year old was a decent fourth in Group 3 company at this meeting last year and often aimed high his fitness could be worth taking on trust.

Awarded the race in the stewards' room after staying on for second last time out at Doncaster over today's trip. Versatile ground-wise and looks a massive price for each-way betting if reproducing that form from just two weeks ago.

TWO TEMPTING shouldn't be discounted so readily here. Had some good runs last season in races of this nature, including nailing one at Chester. Only a couple of pounds higher in the weights here and is considered as this looks a slightly softer touch than some of those, so maybe he can fare better than the Lincoln for an in-form yard.
This horse was a very talented 2-year-old before being mainly disappointing last season. Showed glimpses of form on his final outing last season, and if back in form, looks well handicapped.

My big priced gamble of the day comes in the form of GREAT ACCLAIM at 25/1 with 4 places on offer. I really like the angle of E Johnson Houghton 4yo outsiders (15% SR, A/E 2.15) and this son of Aclaim has shown that he’s a hardy sort; notching up four wins and two places from ten outings last season. He’s 4/7 (A/E 3.99) over a mile on turf, including here at Newbury back in June, and while the gelding is rated 20lb higher today he’s been on an upward trajectory. The break doesn’t concern me given his reappearance run last year, Acclaim’s 20% SR (A/E 1.64) with progeny returning off 150+ days away and the trainer tends to have them ready in Spring for their first run of the year.
Made an eye-catching debut when running on at the finish to take 3rd spot. That outing suggested that this extra furlong could suit this one well this afternoon at decent odds.

Mighty Boy looked promising on debut in France but hasn’t kicked on yet and didn’t seem to stay the trip at Goodwood last time. He’s back from a break now and still lightly raced, so not one to write off just yet. With Bet365 not keen to lay him or slow to adjust their odds, there could be something under the radar here if he’s progressed at home.

Metallo was a bit too close to the pace at Chelmsford last time and didn’t finish off, but he had been in solid form before that. The trainer’s in good nick and the jockey combo has been profitable (19 runs, 4 wins, 1.33 A/E, +16pts @ 83% ROI), so with a more patient ride, he’s got a decent chance of bouncing back.
Rockit Tommy has a solid record with 2 wins from 3 distance runs and previous class success. David Probert's guidance enhances his chances on similar going.
With 10 runners, I'm happy to give each way. The horse thrives this time of year and loves the good ground. As long as the horse jumps well, the horse is handicapped well. 16/1 is great value.

Mel Rowley and Charlie Deutsch are a fairly decent partnership when they link up, and they do so twice on this card at Bangor. Sweet Street is a good ground horse who has won in the past. This isn't a strong race, and I think Sweet Street can run much better than the current odds suggest.
Gwennie May Star has run six times, winning one of them. Looks sure to have a chance here if it can stay the extra two furlongs. Stamina could play a big part.

Handicap debutant Little Dipper looks a big price here. Mel Rowley's 5yo didn't appear to get home at Southwell last month & the drop back to 2miles on good ground looks to be a plus. It's interesting Charlie Deutsch looks to be keen to ride again.

This horse ran well over C&D last time out after a break and was unlucky in running late on. Up in class but getting 8lbs or more from the serious competitors in the field, this horse could pull off a first career win if this hasn't come too soon.

Won over C&D last time out, appreciating the return to the smaller obstacles. Won with more in hand than the official margin suggests and from only 4lb higher could easily still be well enough treated to go in again.

Cables Queen showed a bit on debut when second at Leicester, beaten 5 lengths in a fair novice. She’s been off a while and now drops in trip, which could sharpen her up, while the yard also have a good record in novice races (24 runs, 3 wins, 6 places, 1.13 A/E, +15pts @ 64% ROI)
Made a vast improvement last time out when only just being beaten by a neck. A repeat of that sort of run should see this one involved again at the finish.

Corniche Girl is well bred by Dandy Man out of a useful 9f mare and comes from a yard that knows how to ready one, and while 5f might be a bit on the sharp side on debut, it wouldn’t be a shock if she shows up well with ability in the family.

Time Patrol looked like he had a bit up his sleeve when getting up late at Newcastle and can probably be forgiven his latest run given the poor trip. He’s back on quicker turf now which suits, and the trainer-jockey combination has shown profit in turf handicaps to date (100 runs, 17 wins, 1.07 A/E, +9pts @ 9% ROI).
A former course and distance winner off a 2-pound higher mark and likely to welcome the drop in trip after racing over 7 furlongs at Lingfield last month.

Anglesey Lad had a rough trip last time and didn’t get much luck early or late, so worth putting a line through that. He wasn’t beaten far on his two runs before that and while he’s yet to show his best, the yard’s in form and does well in handicaps at Brighton (47 runs, 8 wins, 1.16 A/E, +14pts @ 30% ROI). Unproven on quick ground, but there’s enough to suggest he could sneak a place if things go smoother.

I can't resist a small win bet on this one, which is likely to put in an all-or-nothing type performance, I suspect. This joint bottom weight has been 2nd in both her attempts over C&D (off 66 and 50), and the 4yo races off just 46 here. The jockey is also somewhat of a specialist at this tricky course. He has one of his best strike rates at the course, and the horse is drawn well to get away with a quick break and attempt to hopefully bag a good position just in behind the leaders. Looks way overpriced on the evidence of those two C&D runs.

One course appearance and one win. This time he is upped 2 furlongs, which should suit and can give the trainer a sort of localish winner. Pat Cosgrave takes the mount, and he is a much underrated jockey. Money on.

Macari did the job nicely over hurdles at Plumpton last time and was on the up when last seen on the Flat. He’d probably prefer a bit of ease underfoot, but his overall profile makes him a solid value shout here, especially with this yard often going under the radar in the market (201 runs, 34 wins, 1.21 A/E, +25pts @ 12% ROI).

Ex-Irish Annexation looks to me like a bit of handicap project. He has been busy on the all weather getting fit. Last time out, having slipped to a mark of 68, he ran a cracker to finish fourth in a 19 runner handicap at Doncaster (slightly inconvenienced near the winning post). That was a most encouraging return to turf. His mark remains unchanged and he carries just 8-10 after allowing for the jockey's claim. Provided he handles the track, Annexation is a most interesting runner for Tony Carroll's yard.
Lexington Knight won here off a 77 last August on GF and comes back today off a 72 on GF, which I think puts him in with a chance.

Luna Effect ran a solid race last time when just touched off at Lingfield and looks to have found his level around this sort of mark. Drops back in trip here and is unproven on quick ground, but he’s lightly raced and may still have a bit more to come. Trainer and jockey combo do well in handicaps (207 runs, 32 wins, 1.07 A/E, +10pts @ 5% ROI), so he’s definitely a player if things fall right.

Top-weight and favourite, Seraphic, is returning from hurdling and this may be a shock to the system. A chance is taken on course specialist Irezumi being race-fit, as the vibes seem quite positive. He acts on good to firm and is on fair racing weight. His regular rider, who has won on him before, can claim 5 pounds so he races off just 8-9. Sawgrass could be a different proposition on handicap debut for owner-breeders Arbib.

Mason Paetel is a jockey on the way up and takes off 7lb here, giving Khangai a good chance of taking this. James Owen does not send many here, but all have a chance when they come to the seaside. Over the winter, Khangai has been in fine form, so hope springs eternal he goes well again.

Didn't show much in three runs for a mark, but they all came in a five-week spell earlier in the year. Half-brother won on his handicap debut earlier in the week, and she may well be capable of doing the family double now that she enters this level. Yard has an excellent record when they send runners to this track.

Shaw Park brings race-fit credentials and reliable mid-tier consistency to this Class 5 field. Statistically well ahead of several rivals and well-placed tactically, his previous runs suggest he’s primed to deliver a big effort. Ground and trip suit perfectly, and he’s expected to handle pressure in the finish.

Won back-to-backs last summer on good/firm going. Unplaced when last seen at Epsom on heavy going. 4-year-old can progress. Chance in competitive small field for trainer with a good record at Brighton.

Blenheim Star wasn’t at her best at Yarmouth last time, but she’s a dual C&D winner on fast ground and tends to go well fresh. With a yard having a strong record at the track (41 runs, 9 wins, 1.27 A/E, +13pts @ 33% ROI) and conditions in her favor, she looks the pick on balance of form and could be set for a big run.

Marsh Benham is a triple C&D winner here and did win after a break when on debut for this yard, way back when. While he tends to do his winning with a bit more give in the ground than today, he has won here on GF in the past and is worth a shot.

Embarked ran a solid race at Yarmouth last time, beaten just a length and a half off 49, and looks primed to strike. He goes well on fast ground, the yard’s in form, and they’ve got a strong record with handicappers at Brighton (47 runs, 8 wins, 1.16 A/E, +14pts @ 30% ROI). Big chance if he runs to that level again.

I tend to follow horses with form at Brighton, and Hellavapace loves it here and is handicapped to go close here under Olivia, who has won and placed on him before. Solid performer in this class at this course under this jockey and ticks all boxes.

Karl Burke has the short-price favorite here, and there has to be a fair chance his filly will be good enough on debut. However, I think the once-raced Filly Foden might just be up to winning. She was second at Musselburgh on her first start behind what looked like a fairly smart filly of Hugo Palmer's. That experience should stand her in good stead here.
Mount Athos made all when winning at Kempton's polytrack surface last month and looks poised to follow those same tactics today.

Bought for a huge 90k last season, he now makes his first appearance for Michael Appleby. Take note of the movers to his yard and the improvements made. I think Kodi Lion is a cut above this class, and if fit enough, he will win.
Kept on inside the final furlong when winning over this trip at Doncaster at the end of last month. Likely to improve further following that race on second run following wind surgery.

On the evidence of this horse's win on his debut start for Michael Dods last time out, you'd have to say that it's pretty conclusive that he looks to have improved the horse, and he can go in again here at a generous-looking 9/1. He's 4lb higher now, but the runner-up only went down by a short head on his next start off a 3lb higher mark. The same jockey keeps the ride, and Thirsk is the course where the trainer has had the most winners in the last year (decent strike rate too).

Small eachway tip for this horse, the trainer has another horse in this race who is better fancied at the odds but I'm not ruling out this one. It's the early part of the turf season but horses from this yard have already been running well so that's encouraging, the trainer often does well at this course which is also encouraging. The selection returns from a rest but did run well first time out last season, wasn't at best form on Soft ground conditions final run of last season but I'm not sure the soft ground conditions were ideal , good ground or better has been more suitable for this horse and he gets those conditions today. Quite an open looking race this so, from a decent draw i think this horse is worth a look as an eachway contender.

TOUCHWOOD is given due consideration back on the turf after taking a decent step forward from a big price on the all-weather last time out. He returns to this sphere lighter in the weights than he was when just missing out at Doncaster last August. Seems OK in this grade and difficult to rule out. Has a handy draw and a pace to aim at.

I think this is a tricky race with Baltic and Arrange dangerous. I also think that this price is false and he should be lower in the betting than this. 9/2 would be about right. Lady La Fay makes her seasonal debut, but there are many questions still to be answered about her as she has only run a handful of times in her career. If she settles, then she will relish the 12f and can ask questions of the others.

The second C Rodriguez mount I like the look of this evening is BALTIC at 5/1. Majestic Warrior is far too short given his poor FlatStats rating and Churchill’s 18% SR (A/E 0.49) with favourites coming up in class, meanwhile Lady La Fay’s FS rating isn’t much better and she has to shoulder Camelot’s 10% SR (A/E 0.45) with fancied runners in 4yo+ races. Arrange could prove to be the fly in the ointment but Baltic looks suited to a steadily run contest like he should get today and just gets the nod over the mare. The son of Frankel is 4/5 over this trip, 5/7 with cheekpieces and while this is his first go at this level he’s shown enough ability with 5 wins on the spin during the middle part of his career. Rodriguez’s 34% SR (A/E 1.33) on fancied runners over long trips and 25% SR (A/E 1.27) on fancied runners in C1-3 races adds further confidence.

Since his last win he has participated in 19 races without success. His form has been largely disappointing, although the conditions at Chester during his last race may not have suited him. The 6-year-old shouldn't be dismissed just yet, an each-way bet at 22/1 could be a smart move if he manages to regain his competitive edge.

5th of 9 but only beaten by three-quarters of a length at Kempton over 7 furlongs when last seen 59 days ago. That was in an apprentice race where he led until close to home. The return of the more experienced Alastair Robinson to the saddle, combined with the drop in trip, appeals.

Plenty to like about Emerald Army running in this big field handicap off 54, with his form sticking out like a sore thumb. His last run posted a really smart time compared to his mark, likely why the form is working out so well. Overnight Oats, who just pipped him last day, is now running off 76. Ran over C&D before, where he finished a creditable 4th/13, but that was his run over 6f, leaving him plenty unexposed for this contest.

It can often pay dividends to back a horse that's performed well off much higher marks and slipped down the handicap due to poor runs but then having had a wind op which might just work the oracle and return them back to form again. That's the possible scenario that could be played out here with this horse down to just 55 but last Summer he was running off marks in the mid 60s and was indeed placed off 66. At the prices, it could be worth chancing that the wind op has done the trick and he could cause a surprise.
Course winner here, which gives her an advantage. The ground conditions, if drying through the day, will play into her hands also. I think Calafrio at 16/1 is a danger here.

John Kirkup has not been so good with all runs on the AW since the break, but I think the return to turf could bring him back in now on a mark of 46, having run to second on turf last August off a 50. EW 5P.

Didn’t get a clear run when 7th of 12 over 7 furlongs at Newcastle on their tapeta surface last month. He will come on for that run following a 144 day break, welcome the drop in trip and represents an in-form Jessica Macey with 2 winners from her last 6 runners.
Decent performer a couple of years ago. Not clicked for new stable yet, but massive drop in weights today. Jockey only going for this one mount. Trip and ground should suit.
Considered a veteran these days. However, he showed up at Wolverhampton in February 2/8 and did win back in December. On a reduced mark for the turf and in with an each-way shout.

Horses 5 , 3 and 7 appear as the more interesting contenders in this, I'll take a chance with Mr Cool who spent most of last season running in better races than this, he may well find this a bit easier than those races last year. Today is just his 2nd run back from a rest so may improve with that last run behind him, did run well on the AW last time where he left the impression he'd do better next time out , back on turf today won't be a problem. Current rating looks fair, a top jockey is booked and the horse is drawn well.
3-year-old filly makes her handicap debut on turf. Judging by her last run, 1/9 at Wolverhampton, there is reason to be optimistic for an each way bet.

Toby Tops looked right at home over 2m when winning well at Southwell last time and the same trip on turf should be fine if he brings that form across. The jockey booking adds confidence and with things falling into place, he looks a serious threat again.

Run With It took a step forward from debut to get off the mark at Southwell, just doing enough to get the job done. He’s up in class here so will need to find more, but the trainer’s in good form and he’s going the right way, so he’s not without a squeak.

Bobacious shaped with promise on her return from a break at Yarmouth, beaten 5 lengths but keeping on well late. She was in solid form before that, generally consistent, and looks likely to come on for the run. With the yard going well early season, especially with last time out winners (59 runs, 13 wins, 1.17 A/E, +18pts @ 30% ROI) , she’s a big player if building on that reappearance.

Judging by its last two outings, this one is on the improve, finishing runner-up in both. Still unexposed, this one has only three runs so far and looks capable of breaking its maiden tag in this race.

Whizz By has been on the up recently, running a strong race at Kempton when just beaten a length off 68, and the step up in trip could suit with how he travelled there. He’s shown he handles turf and with the yard boasting a profitable record at Nottingham (22 runs, 6 wins, 1.89 A/E, +23pts @ 105% ROI), he sets a fair standard and looks the one to beat if continuing that progress.

Manila Thriller didn’t get home over 10f here last time but looked a lot happier over shorter distances previously. So, dropping back in trip is a big plus. The trainer’s in form, and he’s on a generous mark based on earlier efforts. He might just need this after the break, but it wouldn’t be a shock if he outran his price back over preferred conditions, considering the yard shows profit at the course (551 runs, 83 wins, 1.00 A/E, +19pts @ 3.5% ROI).
Yet to set the world alight. However, he is from a top yard, and with a top jockey on top today, he could surprise a few making his handicap debut.

Runner-up in a far deeper race than this one at Doncaster on his return to turf just two weeks back. Is able to run from the same mark here which is more than fair on that effort. He has only won once but that was from a pound higher so is well enough treated if he can find that level of form again.

Fifty Sent has spent all this year running on the AW, with the latest run being a C6 win off a 47 and only up 2 lbs for that. It's worth a shot that he can go as well back on turf with Billy still in the saddle.

Edvard Grieg was well backed last time and ran a decent race at Chelmsford, shaping as though this step back up in trip could help. He showed a bit more earlier in the year on the AW and ran a good second here last summer, so he’s clearly got a liking for the track. With the yard profitable in turf handicaps, he’s one to keep on side.

Hostelry has immediately caught my attention here was last seen at Southwell 32 days ago where finishing 9th/12 however that was her return run after a 154 day break now returning to a suitable turf track with ideal ground conditions and is likely to be much fitter and a lot alert with that run on the all weather under her belt Mrs R Carr's mare is more than capable of bouncing back to form here currently operating on an extremely dangerous mark of 53 Hostelry looks poised to strike here and worth noting she is now operating a total of 10lb below her last winning mark in a race that should be run to suit given the horses enrolled to run here jockey Kaiya Fraser takes off a handy 3lb here which only enhances her good looking claims here price at the time of writing represents decent value and must be taken seriously and accordingly

Back From Dubai was below his usual standard at Wolverhampton but is generally a consistent sort and the drop back in trip should suit much better. Turf form stacks up well alongside his AW efforts, and with the yard strong in early season handicaps (86 runs, 10 wins, 1.15 A/E, +22pts @ 26% ROI), he’s a definite contender if back to his usual self.
